steps.body: The **median** is the middle value — but only of the **sorted** list. Take 7, 2, 9, 4, 6. Sort it first: 2, 4, 6, 7, 9. Five values is an **odd** count, so one value stands exactly in the middle: **6**, with two values below it and two above. Skip the sort and you'd grab the 9 sitting mid-list — not a middle at all.
Build the data on a number line so order becomes visible.

widget.prompt: Build a dot plot for 9, 2, 7, 4. The number line will place the values in order so you can see the middle pair.
widget.successFeedback: The plot orders the values as 2, 4, 7, 9. With four values, the median lies between the two middle points, 4 and 7.
widget.partialFeedback: Each number in the data set needs one dot above its position. Use the number line, not the order in which the values were listed.

predict.prompt: Can you spot the MEDIAN of a list without sorting it first?

options.label: No — middle means middle of the ORDERED list
Yes — take the middle as written

predict.reveal: The median is the middle by SIZE, not by position on the page — sorting first is the non-negotiable move.

explanationVariants: Sorted, the data reads 2, 4, 6, 7, 9. With 5 values (odd), the single middle is the 3rd one: 6, leaving two values on each side.
Cross off ends in pairs — 2 with 9, then 4 with 7 — and the survivor, 6, is the median.

widget.prompt: Find the MEDIAN of 7, 2, 9, 4, 6. (Careful — it isn't sorted yet.)

commonErrors.feedback: 9 is the middle of the UNSORTED list 7, 2, 9, 4, 6 — the classic trap. Sort first (2, 4, 6, 7, 9); the true middle is 6.
7 is one position past the middle — with 5 sorted values, the middle is the 3rd (6), with exactly two values on each side.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Sort: 2, 4, 6, 7, 9. Five values → the 3rd one, 6, is the median.

hints: What must happen before you look for the middle?
Five values — the 3rd from either end.

steps.body: **Even** counts have no single middle — two values share the center, and the median is the **mean of those two**. Sorted data 3, 5, 8, 12, 14, 16 has 6 values; the middle pair is 8 and 12, so the median is (8 + 12) ÷ 2 = **10**. Like the mean, a median can be a number that never appears in the data.
Which pair sits in the center?

widget.prompt: For the sorted data 3, 5, 8, 12, 14, 16 — which TWO values are the middle pair?

options.label: 8 and 12
options.feedback: Yes — two values sit below them (3, 5) and two above (14, 16); the center pair is 8 and 12.

options.label: 3 and 16
options.feedback: Those are the ENDS of the list, not its center. Cross off ends in pairs and 8 with 12 are the last two standing.

options.label: 12 and 14
options.feedback: That pair sits off-center — it leaves three values below and only one above. Balance demands 8 and 12.

explanationVariants: Six values is an even count, so no single value is central. The middle pair is 8 and 12; their mean, (8 + 12) ÷ 2 = 10, is the median.
Cross off in pairs from both ends: 3–16, then 5–14, leaving 8 and 12. Split the difference: 10.

widget.prompt: What is the MEDIAN of the sorted data 3, 5, 8, 12, 14, 16?

commonErrors.feedback: 8 is only ONE of the two middle values. With an even count, average the pair: (8 + 12) ÷ 2 = 10.
12 is only ONE of the two middle values. With an even count, average the pair: (8 + 12) ÷ 2 = 10.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Even count → mean of the middle pair: (8 + 12) ÷ 2 = 10.

hints: Six values — is there a single middle?
The median is the mean of that pair.

explanationVariants: Jae skipped the sort — the middle of an unsorted list is meaningless. Sorted (2, 4, 7, 9), the middle pair is 4 and 7, giving median (4 + 7) ÷ 2 = 5.5.
Order first, middle second: without the sort, position in the list says nothing about size.

widget.prompt: Jae finds the median of 9, 2, 7, 4 by averaging 2 and 7 — 'the two middle numbers.' The right answer is 5.5. What went wrong?

options.label: Jae never sorted — the middle pair of the SORTED list 2, 4, 7, 9 is 4 and 7
options.feedback: Exactly — sorted, the center pair is 4 and 7, and (4 + 7) ÷ 2 = 5.5. The sort is not optional.

options.label: Jae should have used three middle numbers, not two
options.feedback: An even count always centers on exactly two values — the miss was averaging the unsorted list's mid-positions instead of sorting first.

options.label: Nothing — 4.5 and 5.5 are both acceptable medians
options.feedback: A data set has exactly one median. 4.5 came from an unsorted list; only the sorted middle pair (4 and 7) gives the true median, 5.5.

hints: What's the required first move for any median?
Then average the true middle pair, 4 and 7.

explanationVariants: Sort: 2, 4, 7, 9. Four values (even) → middle pair 4 and 7 → median (4 + 7) ÷ 2 = 5.5.
Pair off the ends (2 with 9), leaving 4 and 7 at the center; halfway between them is 5.5.

widget.prompt: Four plants measure 9, 2, 7, and 4 inches tall. What is the MEDIAN height? (Decimals allowed.)

commonErrors.feedback: 4.5 averages 2 and 7 — the mid-POSITIONS of the unsorted list. Sort first: 2, 4, 7, 9; the true middle pair is 4 and 7, median 5.5.
7 is one of the two central values, not the median itself. Even count → average the pair: (4 + 7) ÷ 2 = 5.5.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Sort to 2, 4, 7, 9; even count, so average the middle pair: (4 + 7) ÷ 2 = 5.5 inches.

steps.body: The middle of the lined-up data.
takeaways: Sort first, always — the median is the middle of the ORDERED list.
Odd count: the single central value. Even count: the mean of the middle pair.
The median only cares about position, not size — a fact that becomes its superpower next.

concept.body: Quick rewind. **Sort, then take the middle.** Data 5, 1, 3 sorts to 1, 3, 5 — three values, so the single middle, 3, is the median.

explanationVariants: Sorted: 1, 3, 5. The middle of three values is the 2nd: 3.
Cross off the ends (1 and 5); the survivor, 3, is the median.

commonErrors.feedback: 1 is the middle of the UNSORTED list 5, 1, 3. Sort first — 1, 3, 5 — and the middle is 3.
5 is the largest value, not the middle. Sorted (1, 3, 5), the central value is 3.

widget.fallbackFeedback: Sort to 1, 3, 5; the middle of three values is 3.
